title: One Rule per Action
summary: A rule matches one contract, one action and one call type, and names one policy.
lesson: Each action has at most one rule, and that rule's single policy decides.
oneLiner: A rule matches one contract, one action and one call type, and names one policy.
explain: Each row of the rulebook names a contract, an action and a call type. Almost every call is a normal call.
Change the contract or the action, and the rule no longer applies.
A rule names exactly one policy, the checker that decides. One action never gets two policies, so a co-signer on another row cannot help it.
takeaway: Each action has at most one rule, and that rule's single policy decides.

steps.label: Pay Dave 500 USDC
steps.note: Sending USDC has a rule, and Dave is on its list.

steps.label: Approve Dave to spend 500 USDC
steps.note: Same contract, different action. Letting someone spend USDC has no rule.

steps.label: Send Erin 100 SAFE, co-signed
steps.note: Sending SAFE has its own rule, and that rule asks for the co-signer.

steps.label: Pay Erin 500 USDC, co-signed
steps.note: The USDC rule names the allowlist alone. The co-signer does not count there, and Erin is not on the list.
